items.title: MORE FUEL FOR THE COMMODITY PRICE SUPER CYCLE.
items.content:
MORE FUEL FOR THE COMMODITY PRICE SUPER CYCLE.
 x.com/mining/status/21006991… MINING.COM (@mining)Data centre capacity could exceed 100 GW by 2030, almost double today's base, the World Economic Forum says.

Each megawatt built embeds 72 tonnes of metals and minerals.

Iron, copper, aluminium and graphite carry 98% of that weight, copper at 11,600 kg per MW.

Cooling systems hold 35 to 45% of that mass, backup power 20 to 30%. Servers and chips account for 12 to 16%.

Large power transformers now take two to three years to procure, against weeks before 2020. Backup generators run one to two years.

By 2035 data centres are projected to take 6.0% of global gallium demand, the largest share of any mineral tracked. 

Source: World Economic Forum—  https://x.com/mining/status/2100699197246943529 
— Steve Hanke (@steve_hanke) Sep 19, 2026
